decisions.reason: As a healthcare and hospitality recruitment service it is far from the firm's maritime knowledge base, so despite remaining listed the weak fit with its absorptive capacity makes redeploying resources to maritime-focused offerings more likely.
Superyacht crew recruitment extends the firm's established crewing capabilities into an adjacent niche that management can understand, staff and improve with existing maritime know-how.
The maritime education programme fits the firm's training network and early evidence of six partner institutions soon after launch suggests the firm can assimilate demand and build it further.

Emissions monitoring and compliance services are very close to core ship management and the reported on-time submission of all FuelEU plans shows strong execution and learning in a regulation-driven market.
The emissions compliance dashboard builds directly on the firm's digital ship-management systems and its integration into PAL makes it a complementary capability that should be retained.

The emissions compliance cost simulation tool uses the same regulatory and software knowledge as the dashboard and strengthens client decision support, so a large maritime manager with in-house R&D is likely to continue it.
